context: The low-temperature part of the TDIF curves (Fig. 4) shows step-by-step annealing of deformation-induced defects at different annealing temperatures below the recrystallization onset temperature and follow the same trend as that seen from the independent DSC measurements (Fig. 4, right ordinate). The TDIF curves for the as-deformed ECAP Ni reveal two effects associated with the P1 and P2 peaks. The first effect (P1) disappears after annealing at 400K for 3 days. No changes of the initial UFG microstructure are observed after such annealing treatment and the difference in the corresponding calorimetric signals (Fig. 4) is mainly attributed to annihilation of deformation-induced vacancies, following the reasoning in Ref. [17]. According to the microhardness data (Fig. 2b), the hardness increases with annealing time at 400K due to additional pinning of dislocations by vacancy clusters. The dislocation pinning also inhibits the damping capability of UFG Ni and the peak P1 , seen in as-deformed Ni, disappears after such heat treatment.
